newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Gingrich stands by U.S. pledge to defend Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich stands by U.S. pledge to defend Taiwan.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich on Wednesday reiterated his pledge that the United States would help defend the island, but urged Taiwan and China to refrain from resolving their differences through force.

"It's important to be explicit with both the People's Republic of China and Taiwan that should Beijing seek to reunify Taiwan with the mainland by force or intimidation, the United States will use all means necessary to prevent it," Gingrich said after meeting Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui.

"The use of force or engaging in provocative actions by either side is unacceptable," Gingrich said at an airport news conference, reiterating a position that he said he had expressed in meetings with the leaders of China and Taiwan.
He called on Taipei and Beijing to resume a dialogue that Beijing froze in mid-1995 over suspicions that Taiwan was abandoning its pledge to reunify and was seeking independence from the mainland.

"It is in the interest of those on both sides of the (Taiwan) Strait to resume this process along with a whole range of enhanced social and economic interaction as the best available mechanism for achieving a long-term, peaceful resolution of the differences," he said.

Gingrich heaped praise on Taiwan's economic prowess and its dramatic political development, saying the island had "completed the remarkable journey to full democracy" by electing its parliament and even its president through popular suffrage.

"We will leave here today, based on our conversations with the elected leadership, with a strong renewal of our sense of both the political and economic progress of Taiwan," Gingrich said moments before ending his three-hour visit.
